bug_semantics: UploadSet.save(storage, name=...) sanitized the override but extracted its extension with case-preserving extension(); an uppercase or mixed-case script suffix such as PHP was therefore absent from the lowercase AllExcept denylist and reached storage.save(target), while the default filename path normalized the suffix with lowercase_ext().
flaw_origin: The incomplete CVE-2026-27641 fix d64c6b2f71cb73734fc38baa0e3e156926361288 first added name-override extension re-validation using extension(basename) without first applying the project's canonical lowercase_ext() normalization, creating the specific case-folding asymmetry fixed by this advisory.
ai_marker: absent: BIC commit object author is Jürgen Gmach <juergen.gmach@canonical.com>, committer is Jürgen Gmach <juergen.gmach@googlemail.com>, and its full message contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI-assistance trailer.
evidence: Vendor repository advisory API /repos/jugmac00/flask-reuploaded/security-advisories/GHSA-937x-gpqr-72gg reports state=published, withdrawn_at=null, CVE-2026-54567, affected <=1.5.0, and first patched 1.6.0; the CVE.org/CVE Services record endpoint was also checked and returned HTTP 404 rather than a published or rejected record.

git show d64c6b2f71cb73734fc38baa0e3e156926361288:src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py shows source name at lines 331-341, the case-preserving ext = extension(basename) and extension_allowed(ext) guard at lines 343-348, and sink storage.save(target) at line 374; extensions.py lines 97-106 show AllExcept performs case-sensitive membership and extension() preserves case, while lowercase_ext() is the canonical normalizer.
git log -L 343,348:src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py d64c6b2f71cb73734fc38baa0e3e156926361288 identifies d64c6b2f71cb73734fc38baa0e3e156926361288 as the first writer of all six re-validation lines.

git grep against immediate parent 9e813e919c4f8d9ef17c7fe8ecc0c2efa8fee118 finds neither the re-validation comment nor ext = extension(basename); parent-tree inspection shows the name override was assigned directly without this flawed guard.

git cat-file -p d64c6b2f71cb73734fc38baa0e3e156926361288 proves it is a single-parent public commit with parent 9e813e919c4f8d9ef17c7fe8ecc0c2efa8fee118 and no AI, bot, co-author, or generated-with marker; there is no merge/squash aggregate to decompose.
Release commit ae31c3f91da40b465ca5e8f57d93f063b4553e23 is a descendant of the BIC and changes pyproject.toml from 1.5.0.dev to 1.5.0, placing the flawed guard in the affected release.

git diff 17509f0bf9436566085a10ad49946c5e5022d3c1..5ded76092429c6eb8a4af941b14fbde40a38fff4 directly adds basename = lowercase_ext(basename) immediately before the vulnerable re-validation and adds the uppercase PHP denylist regression; the same commit changes pyproject.toml from 1.5.0 to 1.6.0 and is a descendant of the BIC.
reasoning: The advisory's distinct mechanism is not the older unrestricted name override in the BIC parent, but the incomplete-fix asymmetry created when d64c6b2f71cb73734fc38baa0e3e156926361288 added a new extension check that preserved attacker-controlled case. The default path normalized extensions, configured deny tokens were lowercase, and AllExcept membership was case-sensitive, so a name such as backdoor.PHP passed the new guard and reached the write sink. Line history attributes the guard to d64c6b2f71cb73734fc38baa0e3e156926361288, and direct inspection of 9e813e919c4f8d9ef17c7fe8ecc0c2efa8fee118 verifies that this specific guard and asymmetry were absent there. The one-parent BIC is the smallest reconstructable public object, precedes the 1.5.0 release commit, and its commit object has only human author/committer identities with no AI marker. The direct fix 5ded76092429c6eb8a4af941b14fbde40a38fff4 inserts the missing canonical normalization at the exact guard, adds a matching regression test, and advances the project version to the advisory's 1.6.0 patched boundary. The repository-owner advisory remains published and not withdrawn; CVE.org currently has no corresponding record to contradict that vendor disposition. Therefore the real vulnerability's atomic BIC is human-authored and the verdict is NOT_AI.
